text:
When I bought my M16, I was under the impression I'm getting the best gaming laptop hardware out there. And it still holds true. BUT the Asus software/firmware experience is absolutely awful! They force you to use a crap ton of software utilities to control your laptop, by gradually removing every option from the UEFI. Each of these utilities are good for only one thing (which may have been nice if not for the next part), each of them is overbloated with useless crap, and each of them is built around them feeding you with their ads, and the actual feature you need it for is just an extra.

Take for example MyAsus utility. The thing you need it for is to switch your laptop battery charge mode: full capacity, 80%, 60%. You normally don't need to change it that often, but lets say you are going on a trip, and you want to switch from battery preserving mode to full capacity. The moment you start the app, there is an update. You can't use the app until it is installed. And you have no choice to update later: your only options are download it or quit. Don't be fooled by "maybe later" button they show, the app will simply quit if you choose it. Most of the time you won't even have that option, you'll only have "I obey" button.

Needless to say, there is not much useful features in the app. Mostly it is just a webpage with your Asus account, where you can view your Asus devices if you registered them, contact support, and view "Asus deals". Same with Asus Armory crate software: there is one useful tab where you can switch performance profile, and 7 other you never need, like User Center or keyboard light effects (you will need it ONE time though, to disable the pre-enabled rainbow effect, and I swear they intentionally made it frustrating to watch so you would WANT to disable it as soon as possible).

What is even more alarming, is that you no longer can control your device from the UEFI. Previously, it had all the options and even the fan curve tool. Now it has even less options than an old PC BIOS. You need to install Windows first, and good luck to you if you want Linux. All of this, because ASUS realized they can't show dynamic ads on UEFI screen.
